correctness.rationale: Exact degree-four polynomial identity K z^4-(z-mu)^4-A(z-a mu)^2(z-b mu)^2=(10+6 sqrt(3))mu^3(z-mu) integrates to a positive remainder for all real L4 functions. Nearest-root rounding controls its fourth and second errors, the mean enforces distance to measurable event masses, and two deficit regimes give a uniform c delta^2 lower bound. A two-valued witness provides the uniform C delta^2 upper bound. Symbolic algebra, rational polynomial checks, and sampled cases were replayed from the packaged script; samples are not substituted for analytic quantifiers. Equality and boundary cases were checked, including the trivial one-atom space.

evidence: Móri 2009 Theorem 2.1 proves the unrestricted sharp bound by two-point laws but does not quantify attainable-event-mass distance.
Shargorodsky--Sharia 2023 introduction and Theorem 2.1, DOI 10.1002/mana.202100217, establish general centered and conditionally centered moment bounds.
Lewicki--Skrzypek 2016 finite-uniform result is reproduced as formula (1.11) in the 2023 introduction.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general Lp inequality K is strictly weaker than an all-space two-sided norm-deficit formula. A finite-uniform exact norm formula can imply special-case rates but does not control arbitrary atomic mass vectors or mixed measures. The inaccessible original 2016 proof is identified as a residual risk.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The norm of I minus expectation on a real weighted L4 space is the same object as the norm of projection onto its mean-zero hyperplane. Existing minimal-projection constants need not equal this particular projection norm when atomic masses are unequal. The known universal fourth-moment constant is K, whereas the new object is its quantitative probability-space-specific deficit.

originality.rationale: The unrestricted Franchetti fourth-moment constant and Bernoulli optimal profile are acknowledged prior art. The accepted novelty is a universal two-sided quadratic relationship between the actual centering norm loss and distance of the whole probability-space event-mass range to the forced Bernoulli mass, with arbitrary weights and mixed measures. Material comparison of Móri 2009, Aksoy--Lewicki 2010, Shargorodsky--Sharia 2023 and available Lewicki--Skrzypek 2016 descriptions did not show a covering result; original full-text access limitations are retained as risk. No exhaustive priority or independence is asserted.
residual_risks: The original 2016 Lewicki--Skrzypek paper was not materially available in full; a general hyperplane projection statement could imply an unrecognized weighted centering special case.
The original 1990 Franchetti paper was not materially available in full, although its universally sharp benchmark was independently reconstructed and explicitly treated as prior art.
A more general preexisting stability theorem in Banach-space projection theory could imply the same quadratic gap without using event-mass terminology.

value.rationale: For arbitrary probability spaces, the scalar set of attainable event probabilities is a mathematically natural measure-structure invariant. The result classifies exactly when the sharp nonatomic fourth-moment centering norm survives and gives a dimension-free *sharp-order* quantitative defect when it does not. It applies to arbitrary nonuniform atomic weights and mixed measures, rather than a chosen small matrix or recomputed table. The squared order cannot be improved uniformly by the two-atom laws. The exact comparison constants are acknowledged nonoptimal, and no full formula for positive gap is claimed.
